newsitem.title: USA: US mortgage-backeds slip in narrow trading range.
newsitem.headline: US mortgage-backeds slip in narrow trading range.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities retreated from earler gains in a narrow trading range on Tuesday, after a weaker-than-expected 10-year Treasury note auction, traders said.
"The (auction) was not quite as good as people had hoped," said one New York-based trader.
"Personally, I think the market is a little overbought... so I think the natural direction is for rates to come up a little bit," he added.
"(Pass-through) trading is still very narrow," said another New York-based trader, referring to the difference between Treasury and mortgage yields.
"We didn't get much movement one way or the other today and the 10-year (Treasury note) has been trading in a quarter-point range all day."
By late on Tuesday, pass-throughs ranged from 2/32 to 5/32 lower.
Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent coupons were off 4/32 at 99-13/32, yielding 112 basis points over comparable Treasuries.
The 10-year Treasury note was down 4/32 to yield 6.54 percent.
Comparable Fannie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent pass-throughs were down 4/32 at 99-11/32, and FHLMCs were down 2/32 at 99-15/32.
One trader said he saw a few bid lists today and had mentioned a "large buyer of 15-year (Pass-through) paper."
"I don't think it was huge," conceded the trader, adding that it may have been $100 to $150 million.
